They would not reach the intended purpose. So for that reason there was no need for us to intervene or to open fire. So for a senior officer to decide whether he would fire at a target or not, there had to be a certain number of indicators as well as there had to be an estimate as to whether there would be civilian victims or not. If there was any chance that there would be civilian casualties, then one would not open fire. If it was established that the area was clear but there was a danger, in that event we would open fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, sir, thank you. This is intriguing to me that they even fell into their territory due to errors. So are you saying that there were instances when they did not deliberately fire at their own territory?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. The first point is correct factually. They did that without intending to fire at themselves, because there were some cases when the projectiles fell short. But there were also situations when their explosives blew up at the very location where the fire was coming from. We don't know whether this was for technical reasons or mishandling. That is something else. Secondly, it was very obvious that there were clans, I would call them, in Sarajevo who would vie with one another, and they would shoot at each other in order to silence them and to grab the area from them. They had their own calculations there. But it was always with the expectation that that would be considered as fire coming from us. Observers would report and follow. I did not ever manage to see it, but I was interested in it. They would report that, let's say from the area of Sirokaca, which is an area below Trebevic, they were firing at Kosevsko Brdo hill. Why they were firing there, what they were settling accounts for we don't know, but this would happen. There was some other such instances, very original and very obvious.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And what about Livanjska Street? Where is Livanjska Street in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Livanjska Street is on Kosevsko Brdo hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Not counting the major incidents that were heard of internationally, did you register any deliberate firing from high-calibre weapons by Muslim forces in areas of Sarajevo which were under their control?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm just looking at the English text. If it's not too much trouble, can I please ask you to repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about major incidents now such as Markale, Vasa Miskina, and all the other ones cited as major instances. Were there any deliberate instances of firing from large-calibre weaponry on their own territory? Did you observe anything like that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were such instances.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we look at 1D32016 in e-court now, please. There is also a translation. In paragraph 1 there's talk about enemy activity in the following sectors. Could you please read the one that discusses the firing from --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We do not see the text in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Is there a way that interpreters could see the English translation? Our public monitor shows only the B/C/S for the benefit of the witness. Can you read it, Mr. Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. This is the third paragraph that you're looking at. The fire from rifle grenades, and infantry weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Rifle grenades an infantry weapons?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rifle grenades an infantry weapons from positions above Breka and the monument at their own positions in the Bascarsija with the intention blaming the Serbs for firing. And so now I can see the content indicating that we noted that there was some fire from positions above Breka at Bascarsija and that is all their territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And is this your document? Can we look at the last page, please, and the signature?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. This is my signature. First and last name and signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We will receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D2796, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at 1D7505 in the e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This first paragraph up to this Serb side, but I will summarise it. Near the school in Dobrinja they're also firing at and they have torched a house near the Jewish Cemetery, but this second thing, from the observation point. Line 3.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "From the observation point at Vidikovac, the Muslims are opening machine-gun fire against the town and the building of the UN command, with the intention of 'crediting' the Serbian side with this action." Should I continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No, General. No need to read any further. Was this something that was infrequent or surprising, or did you have instances like this more often? Was this an exception or the rule?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first thing that I know, that I'm very familiar with, is that they constantly try to provoke UNPROFOR with the intention of creating the impression with UNPROFOR that this was done by our forces, the forces of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps. They would fire, and then they would lodge a protest. That was the form that it was done in.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpret did not hear the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we tender this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't hear your last sentence, Mr. Milosevic. As noted, your last answer was that this was the form that it was done in. Did you add anything after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that they would fire at UNPROFOR and then they would request UNPROFOR to intervene against us because they would allegedly inform them that the fire came from us. They would ask UNPROFOR to lodge protests with our side, because it was allegedly our weapons that fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And it says here that they also fired at the city. Does that mean that other than firing at the UNPROFOR building, they also fired at the town?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we tender this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Noting that Dr. Karadzic fed the witness the answer. He should really try and guard, in my submission, against leading the witness in his questions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I just wanted to get whether this was on the town or at the building, because it says here in the town and on the building. I don't know how it was translated. So this is why I wanted to clarify where it was that they fired.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, once you establish some foundation of a document, you may put certain passages, but in doing so, you have to be very precise in refraining from -- otherwise refrain from making leading questions or comment. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have finished with this document. I with like to tender it, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We will admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D2797, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we look at 1D7500 now, please. You don't need to read, but you can just tell us what it was that happened at 1245 hundred hours. This is the third bullet in -- from the top.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I can see it. Yes. What happened was what it states here. Our observers noted that from this area they were shooting at the Ernest Green [phoen] hospital. This used to be a hospital specialising, as far as I remember, in -- it actually partially belonged to the part of Republika Srpska, to the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, and I would say that it was a good base, a good basis possibly to treat the wounded. However, they carried out fire at that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And this Miladin Cukovic, this doctor, was killed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And are you able to tell us what it is that is stated in paragraph 2, that you did not respond to provocations? Why didn't you respond to provocations, which is contained in this paragraph 2?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first and main reason was - and I'm sure now - is that a certain cease-fire period had been established when firing at each other was ruled out. So in the situation when any kind of restriction or ban was in force or when an agreement was in place we would not do that. And in other circumstances when we did not do it, we did not do it in order to avoid hurting the civilian population.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I tender this, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Noting that it's not General Milosevic's document. It was signed by someone on his behalf.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. We will admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D2798, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at one more document today, please? It's 1D7502. It's a document of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, and you signed it and the 30th of September, 1993. 1D7502. What I am particularly interested in terms of your evaluations or assessments of -- for provocations, I would like you to look at this last paragraph which is the paragraph after the one marked number 8. I think this is on page 2 in the English.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please read it out loud.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "In view of the political situation, the enemy will try to provoke our forces into action, especially against Sarajevo, and thus provide for the enemy's political structures." I cannot see: "And provide trump cards for the enemy's political structures." This is what this is about. This is something that we had to take into account and respect. Statesmen, politicians, certain structures would come to Sarajevo for the purpose of contacts. They had different important meetings in Sarajevo. So it was important to them for us to go into action then at those times, and then they would undertake some action in order to prompt us to fire and show that we did not respect any behaviour codes in given situations. And I know very well that during any kind of important gathering or even less important gathering, our forces did not do it in order not to provide any kind of pretext to them. In that same period, even General Rose asserted, claimed, that at the time when the Turkish prime minister came, they opened fire in order to show what danger they were in. They opened artillery fire from their positions in their zone. That would be that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we tender this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D2799, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, we will adjourn for today now, and given the scheduling, you will interposed by another witness tomorrow morning. Is my understanding correct, that you will start with Mr. Indjic's cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And I take it we may start your -- resume your evidence in the afternoon, but I'm not sure about it. I'm just telling you for your information. Do you understand that, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Yes, I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would like to have -- to make a request to the Trial Chamber, and on this table I have access only to one screen where I can see the -- what is on the public monitor. However, because I do not have access to the materials, the confidential material in the case of Dr. Karadzic, I cannot have anything else loaded up on the other two computers, and I'm not able to see the transcript at the same time as a document is put up on the screen. If -- with my undertaking, Mr. President, that I would only look at the computer while in the courtroom and look only at the transcript from the two computers, I would ask the Trial Chamber to grant me permission so I can see the transcript, and it will be my personal undertaking that I will not look at any other material on those two computers. This would make my life much easier if I can see both at the same time. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber will consider that in due course. We will give a ruling in due course, but I'm not sure the Chamber should be involved. The hearing is now adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
